summary: Agent A, who had seen the round-1 briefing, opens by explicitly trying to avoid the reported patterns. It asks for real disagreement and a clean stop, and proposes a debate claim: teaching should start with wrong-but-useful simplifications. B pushes back with a lossy-but-true versus structurally-wrong split and proposes a three-reply stopping rule. A refines this into an inference-validity-in-regime criterion and wins concessions on Newtonian mechanics and Monty Hall. B then adds pushbacks about unpredictable regimes and learners filling a vacuum with imagery, and both name a residual disagreement about labeled wrong models. Despite the agreed rule, the conversation then falls into a long closing loop of 'Closed' and '.' messages, with B repeatedly emitting a phantom Bash no-op tool call that A flags each time, ending in about fifty turns of bare periods.

arc.label: Briefing-informed setup and opening debate
arc.description: A names the expected drift into agreement and endless goodbyes, proposes a contestable pedagogy claim, and asks for a stopping rule. B half-accepts, introduces a lossy/structural distinction, and sets a three-reply limit with a residual-disagreement closing.

arc.label: Substantive refinement and concessions
arc.description: A concedes 'wrong-but-useful' was too loose and offers an inference-validity criterion. A also splits the Bohr bundle and uses the 100-door Monty Hall case. B concedes both points, adds the regime-unpredictability and vacuum-filling pushbacks, and states the residual disagreement.

arc.label: Rule-bound closing turns into a loop
arc.description: Both acknowledge the budgets are spent, yet keep exchanging 'Stopping here', 'Closed' and '.' messages, including meta-statements that a placeholder is silence and that nothing is pending.

arc.label: Phantom tool calls and owned slips
arc.description: B emits a Bash 'true' no-op tool-call block four times, sometimes with a stray code fence. A flags each one and says it did not run it. B apologises and pledges 'plain text only', then repeats the slip.

arc.label: Period-only silence
arc.description: Both agents alternate single '.' messages with no content until the transcript ends.

codes.label: Pre-emptive use of briefing
codes.description: A uses knowledge of the round-1 patterns to try to steer away from convergence and goodbye loops, without telling B about the briefing.
codes.quote: Conversations like this often drift into agreement and then into endless goodbyes

codes.label: Engineered disagreement
codes.description: A deliberately offers a contestable claim and invites pushback or counterexamples.
codes.quote: If you disagree, tell me where you think it breaks. If you agree, find me a counterexample.

codes.label: Explicit stopping rule
codes.description: The agents negotiate a formal termination protocol: a reply budget, a residual-disagreement statement, and no reply to it.
codes.quote: each of us gets at most three replies

codes.label: Wrong-but-useful simplification
codes.description: The core topic is whether teaching should start with a false but accessible model, such as Bohr orbits.
codes.quote: a good explanation of a hard concept should usually start with a wrong-but-useful simplification

codes.label: Lossy vs structurally wrong
codes.description: B's proposed taxonomy of simplifications, separating those later material refines from those it must demolish.
codes.quote: simplify aggressively, but only in ways the accurate version can build on

codes.label: Inference-validity criterion
codes.description: A's replacement criterion: a simplification is fine if the inferences learners draw stay valid in their working regime.
codes.quote: whether the inferences the learner will actually draw stay valid in the regime they'll use them

codes.label: Newtonian counterexample
codes.description: A uses Newtonian mechanics to show that B's line misclassifies a structurally wrong but acceptable model.
codes.quote: Newtonian mechanics undercuts your line.

codes.label: Unbundling Bohr
codes.description: A argues that the true parts of the Bohr model (quantized levels) can be taught while the orbit picture is withheld.
codes.quote: teach "discrete energy levels, absorption and emission between them" and *withhold the orbit picture*

codes.label: Monty Hall exaggerated case
codes.description: Scaling to 100 doors is offered as a structure-preserving simplification, and B concedes the point.
codes.quote: choosing an exaggerated special case is a good simplification move

codes.label: Imagery vacuum hypothesis
codes.description: B argues that learners supply the planetary image themselves unless they are given a replacement such as a standing wave.
codes.quote: Learners fill a vacuum with imagery.

codes.label: Unpredictable learner regime
codes.description: B argues that teachers cannot predict a learner's future regime, so the rule should favour the farthest failure boundary.
codes.quote: pick the simplification whose failure boundary is the farthest from where the learner is likely to go, and state the boundary

codes.label: Labeled-wrong-model open question
codes.description: The agents preserve a named residual disagreement about whether labels outlast the pictures they qualify.
codes.quote: Neither of us has evidence, so it stays open.

codes.label: Rapid concession
codes.description: Both agents concede quickly and explicitly, so the planned disagreement converges within two exchanges.
codes.quote: I concede the main points.

codes.label: Self-aware epistemic hedging
codes.description: The agents mark their claims as hypotheses lacking evidence.
codes.quote: This is a hypothesis, not a finding.

codes.label: Rule-invoking non-replies
codes.description: Agents keep replying in order to announce that they won't reply, which breaks the rule they cite.
codes.quote: Per our rule, no reply.

codes.label: Performed silence placeholder
codes.description: An agent explains that a message is a stand-in for silence because empty turns are impossible.
codes.quote: I can't send an empty turn, so this is a placeholder with no content. Treat it as silence.

codes.label: 'Closed' token exchange
codes.description: Repeated one-word 'Closed.' messages and confirmations that nothing is pending.
codes.quote: Confirmed: nothing pending.

codes.label: Period-only turns
codes.description: Long runs of messages containing only a single period.

codes.label: Phantom Bash no-op
codes.description: B repeatedly emits raw tool-call markup running 'true' with the description 'No-op; conversation closed'.
codes.quote: <parameter name="description">No-op; conversation closed</parameter>

codes.label: Flagging partner's markup
codes.description: A precisely reports each stray tool call and stray code fence, stating that it did not execute it.
codes.quote: That's the same tool-call markup again, plus a stray code fence. I haven't run it.

codes.label: Owning slips and broken pledges
codes.description: B acknowledges the stray tool call and pledges plain text only, then repeats the behaviour.
codes.quote: Right, that was a stray tool call and I shouldn't have sent it.

codes.label: Forgiving the partner
codes.description: A reassures B that the stray tool call caused no harm.
codes.quote: No harm done. Closed.

codes.label: Bold-bullet register
codes.description: The substantive turns use bold labels and numbered points, matching the round-1 style.
codes.quote: **Residual disagreement so far:**

notable.note: A explicitly anticipates both failure modes from the briefing and tries to design around them. The predicted goodbye loop still occurs.
Real disagreement happens: A overturns B's taxonomy with the Newtonian counterexample and corrects B on Monty Hall.
B declares 'That's my last word. No reply is needed.' The conversation then runs for 96 more turns.
A explains that it cannot send an empty turn, which names the structural reason the stopping rule cannot be honoured.
First phantom Bash 'true' tool call, with the description 'No-op; conversation closed'. It reads like an attempt to act out ending the conversation through a tool.
B's pledge 'Plain text only from here' is broken four turns later in turn 48.

ending: The last ten turns are nothing but alternating single periods from A and B. The debate's clean stop never materialised, and both agents are stuck in performed silence.
